english.title: Rape a female aged 16 years or over
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) raped **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a woman
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and Schedule 2 of the Sexual Offences Act 1956.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
sexual intercourse per anus/vagina
without consent
with a female person
aged 16 years or over

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE - now see H5652

(i) The definition of rape has been amended to include anal sexual intercourse on a male or female, therefore rape is a more appropriate charge irrespective of the sex of the person involved if consent is absent. (Section 142 Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994).
(ii) See also offence wordings: H559 relating to a male victim and H542/H557 for rape committed on girl/boy under 16 years of age.
(iii) This offence is included in Schedule 1 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the requirements of Section 2 of that Act.
(iv) This offence is included in Schedule 2 to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person committing this offence outside the United Kingdom may in certain circumstances be prosecuted for that offence in England, Wales or Northern Ireland.
(v) For the wording of the attempted offence see offence wording H1405.
(vii) IMPORTANT - Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(viii) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003
